investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409 — agent quota exceeded: limit is 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T03:38:10–13Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the org-level remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap across the entire remote-agents feature eval suite.
investigation.rootCause: The eval probe account's organization has reached the swarm backend's hard limit of 100 remote agents. POST /api/agents returns HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before any agent is provisioned. Because the runner calls createAgent() as the very first substantive step (run-status-probes.mjs line 791), all downstream evidence collection (vmIdPresent, remoteState, agentId) is skipped, and every remote-agents check fails with the same message. This is an eval infrastructure / probe-account resource exhaustion issue; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Probe account org has accumulated 100 remote agents and hit the swarm backend's hard quota ceiling. Prior eval runs may not have cleaned up agents (withCleanup may have failed silently or been interrupted), leaving stale agents counted against the quota.

SECONDARY — The withCleanup wrapper in the runner failed to delete agents from one or more previous eval runs (e.g., due to a runner crash, timeout, or CI cancellation), causing quota to accumulate over time without the probe account being aware.

TERTIARY — The quota limit itself was recently lowered on the swarm backend side (a backend configuration change), causing an org that was previously under the limit to suddenly be over it. No backend config evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit aee54ab ('ci(observability): guard release history publishing') touched workflow files including .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml, which could theoretically have altered cleanup or retry behavior; however, aee54ab's candidateTouchedPaths list contains no eval probe source files and matchedNeedles is empty, so this is a weak hypothesis without additional diff evidence.

This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production swarm API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
